blocking.summary: eval.mjs KEEP_UNREDACTED exempts 'criterion_id' from redaction, but for backlogged findings that key holds the reviewer's raw text (the `later()` path in classify copies f.criterion_id verbatim when it is missing from the contract). A secret env value in a reviewer's criterion_id is therefore written unredacted to both backlog.json and the verdict file (backlogged[]). The run.mjs keep-set has the same key, but only in-contract ids reach it there.

backlogged.summary: KEEP_UNREDACTED in lib/run.mjs is matched by key name at any depth (e.g. 'files', 'title', 'feature', 'history', 'config'). A future nested field with one of those names that holds command output would be saved unredacted. Today none of the verify or state shapes do. Consider limiting the keep-list to top-level paths of the state and result entries.

Redaction covers every non-allowlisted env value of 8 or more characters, so variables such as PWD or OLDPWD also rewrite absolute paths inside the state file. For example, lastVerify.cwd can be saved as '[redacted]/.harness/wt/F34'. Nothing reads these fields back on --resume, so this is only cosmetic, but it can hamper debugging of a saved state.

The F34 tests write records with an injected env, but there is no test for the interactive `harness eval` command, which uses the default env = process.env. The default path is a one-line default parameter, so the risk is low.
Redaction still runs after verify.mjs's tail() has cut the output, so a secret split at the cut boundary leaves an unredacted suffix. This now also applies to the state file and verdicts.

The run.mjs KEEP_UNREDACTED set is key-name based and applies at any depth: 'title', 'files', 'feature', 'history' and 'config' are exempt wherever they appear in state. No path puts command output under those keys today, but a future field with one of those names would silently skip redaction. Consider scoping the exemption to known paths.
Only values of 8 or more characters from the passed env are redacted. Short or transformed secrets still reach the state file, verdicts and backlog (documented in SR-8).
